title: Experiment slate generator & OKR-mapped decision automation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: As experiment volume grows across teams, we lose velocity and spend cycles on low-impact T-tests. Goal: build a lightweight pipeline that (1) generates a recommended experiment slate each cycle prioritized by expected OKR impact and confidence, (2) maps each experiment to one or more OKR/initiative milestones, and (3) wires rule-based decision automation (stat sig thresholds + business-action triggers) to reduce manual ops during rollouts. This ticket scopes the PM work: prioritization formula, minimal UI for owners to accept/override the slate, required telemetry for automated decisions, and ops safeguards (audit log, manual override, cooldown windows).
acceptance_criteria: Prioritization engine implemented as a service that scores candidate experiments by (expected impact * confidence) / cost (proof-of-concept model); output is exportable as CSV/JSON.
Each scoreable experiment can be linked to one or more OKRs and shows projected contribution percentage in the UI.

Decision rules support at least: promote (wider rollout), expand (increase traffic by X%), pause, cancel. Each rule maps to a measurable threshold (p-value, lift, revenue estimate) and audit log entries.
Owners can accept or veto the generated slate via a lightweight UI; vetoed items are tracked with reason and routed to the experiments backlog.
Notifications: Slack + email notifications triggered for Promote/Pause/Cancel actions with links to the experiment dashboard and required escalation steps.
E2E test: simulate 50 candidate experiments and verify the slate generator ranks higher-OKR-impact experiments above low-impact ones 90% of the time (based on seeded input distributions).
comments: 2026-03-01 Ava Chen: Kickoff — aligned with OKR owners (Growth, Reliability). Scope limited to A/B and percentage rollouts for Q2 runway. Decided to exclude multi-variant and model-swap experiments in v1.
2026-03-03 Mateo Alvarez: Shared initial prioritization formula proposal: score = (impact_score * pri_confidence) / sqrt(cost_estimate). Asked Eng to validate cost heuristic for ML-backed features.
2026-03-05 Priya Desai (Eng): Cost heuristic validated against historical runtime/ops data; suggested adding a minimum sample size guard to avoid spurious prioritization of tiny experiments.

2026-03-07 Design review (Liam Park): UI wireframes added to Drive. Emphasize clear OKR mapping and single-click accept/override flow. Avoid showing raw p-values to PMs — show binary pass/fail + contextual lift ranges.

2026-03-09 Security (Nadia Singh): Audit logging + RBAC note — decision automation must require a secondary approver for experiments touching customer data. Marked security_review_required=false for v1 since no sensitive data expected, but flagged for v2.
2026-03-10 Mateo Alvarez: Implementer note — backend proto for scoring service up; working on CSV export and Slack hook. Next: build lightweight UI and wire decision-rule engine to experiment runner.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: scoring service + CSV/JSON export + Slack notification hooks (no auto-action live, only suggested).
Phase 2: UI for owners + accept/override + audit log. Add manual promote/expand/pause actions in the console.
Phase 3: opt-in decision automation with canary safety net (auto-promote when lift>X and p<0.05 and no alert flags).
Safety: every automated action generates an audit entry and a 30-minute cooldown window during which it can be immediately rolled back by oncall.
Monitoring: add a per-experiment health feed (latency, error rate, traffic delta) and tie into SLO alerts.
